c.tagline: La Superba - a maritime maze of palaces, pesto, and the biggest aquarium in Italy.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are white and metered, with fixed surcharges at night and for luggage. Uber offers only its licensed taxi/black-car service in Genoa (no UberX), so most people hail at a rank or book through Free Now or the itTaxi app.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance; 113 reaches the state police and 118 reaches medical emergencies directly.

avoid.reason: Caution in the old-town alleys (caruggi) near the port at night

hood_desc: One of Europe's largest medieval old towns, a labyrinth of narrow caruggi opening onto Piazza De Ferrari and the striped cathedral; atmospheric and packed with trattorias and focaccia bakeries, though some lanes feel edgy after dark.
The Renaissance 'New Streets' of Via Garibaldi, lined with the UNESCO-listed Palazzi dei Rolli and the Musei di Strada Nuova; the grandest, most elegant slice of the historic centre.

The revitalised old port redesigned by Renzo Piano, home to Italy's largest aquarium, the Galata maritime museum, the Bigo lift, and waterfront restaurants; the most family-friendly, walkable base by the sea.

A refined residential district east of the centre with Liberty-style villas, the seafront Corso Italia promenade, and good restaurants; calm and upmarket, popular with families and longer-stay visitors.
A picture-perfect former fishing hamlet of pastel houses around a tiny pebble cove, famous for gelato and sunset views; quiet and romantic, a short bus or shore walk from the centre.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though some locals prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: The metro runs roughly 5:00 AM to 11:30 PM; buses run from early morning to around midnight with a limited night network, and the Zecca-Righi funicular runs into the evening.
transit.note: Genoa's single metro line plus a dense bus network, two funiculars, and a series of public elevators and lifts help conquer the steep hills; the Genova-Casella narrow-gauge railway climbs into the Apennine foothills.
transit.pay: A single AMT ticket is EUR 1.50 and valid 100 minutes across buses, the metro, funiculars, and public elevators; a day pass is about EUR 4.50. Buy from tobacconists, machines, or the AMT app and validate on boarding; contactless tap-and-go is rolling out.

bus: Autostazione Genova (Piazza della Vittoria, Flixbus & intercity)
ferry: Port of Genoa (Stazione Marittima / Terminal Traghetti)

transit.m: Volabus (line 100) to Piazza Principe & Brignole stations (~30 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a cover charge (coperto) is usually on the bill, so rounding up or leaving a euro or two for good service is appreciated but not expected.

food.name: Trofie al pesto genovese
food.desc: Short hand-rolled twists with pesto pounded from Prà basil, pine nuts and pecorino, tossed with potato and green beans as tradition demands.

places.name: Il Genovese
places.note: Restaurant built around Ligurian classics; its mortar-made pesto is the city reference.

places.name: Trattoria Rosmarino
places.note: Homemade pasta and focaccia, with old-port views from the upper tables.

places.name: Trattoria Ugo
places.note: Open since 1969 and almost unchanged; honest Ligurian home cooking at fair prices.

food.name: Focaccia genovese
food.desc: Dimpled, oil-pooled flatbread eaten at any hour, famously dunked in morning cappuccino; sold by weight, warm, straight from the oven.

places.name: Panificio Mario
places.note: Long-standing bakery locals queue at for classic salt-and-oil focaccia.

places.name: Antico Forno Patrone
places.note: Wood-fired neighbourhood forno also doing focaccia with onion and olives.

places.name: Focacceria Priano
places.note: Reliable all-day slices; good stop between the station and the old town.

food.name: Focaccia col formaggio
food.desc: Two paper-thin sheets of dough sealing molten stracchino cheese, blistered in a fierce oven; a Recco speciality adopted across Genoa.

places.name: Trattoria Rosmarino
places.note: Wood-fired oven turning out a Recco-style cheese focaccia alongside farinata.

places.name: Manuelina
places.note: The historic house of focaccia col formaggio, worth the short coastal trip.

places.name: Old-town sciamadde
places.note: Traditional fried-food shops sell it by the slab through the day.

food.name: Farinata di ceci
food.desc: A thin chickpea-flour pancake baked in copper pans until the edges crisp; sold hot by the wedge with black pepper and nothing else.

places.name: Antica Sciamadda
places.note: Copper pans into a wood oven since 1850, one of the last true sciamadde.

places.name: Sa Pesta
places.note: Century-old oven doing farinata, torte di verdura and cima to a loyal crowd.

places.name: Antica Friggitoria Carega
places.note: Standing counter under the arcades for farinata and fried seafood cones.

food.name: Pansoti in salsa di noci
food.desc: Plump triangles stuffed with wild greens and preboggion herbs, blanketed in a creamy pounded walnut sauce rather than meat ragu.

places.name: Trattoria Ugo
places.note: Old-school kitchen where pansotti and walnut sauce are made in house daily.

places.name: C'era una Volta
places.note: Simple, authentic Genoese menu that always keeps pansoti and cod brandade on.

places.name: Cavour Modo 21
places.note: Family-run and busy with locals for pansotti con noci and peppered mussels.

food.name: Cappon magro and Ligurian antipasti
food.desc: The city's baroque layered salad of hardtack, boiled seafood and vegetables under green sauce, plus cima and torta pasqualina.

places.name: Il Genovese
places.note: One of the few kitchens still building the full cappon magro to order.

places.name: Sa Pesta
places.note: Historic spot for cima alla genovese and vegetable tortes at everyday prices.

places.name: Trattoria Rosmarino
places.note: Seasonal Ligurian starters with homemade bread and focaccia to start.

food.name: Ligurian white wine (Vermentino and Pigato)
food.desc: Crisp, saline coastal whites from the Riviera hills that were built for pesto and fried seafood; poured by the glass all over the old town.

places.name: Les Rouges
places.note: Grand frescoed wine bar with a deep Ligurian list and knowledgeable pours.

places.name: Cambi Cafe
places.note: Wine shop and bar in a 200-year-old cellar; strong on small Ligurian growers.

places.name: Enoteca Sola
places.note: Long-established enoteca for tasting Vermentino and Pigato side by side.

food.name: Historic-cafe espresso and hot chocolate
food.desc: Genoa's 19th-century cafes still serve thick cioccolata, espresso and candied-fruit sweets in gilded rooms off the old-town lanes.

places.name: Pasticceria Klainguti
places.note: Trading since 1828; Verdi was a regular, and the pastries live up to it.

places.name: Antica Confetteria Romanengo
places.note: Candied fruit and chocolate maker from 1780, an operating museum piece.

places.name: Caffe Mangini
places.note: Belle-epoque cafe for an unhurried espresso or aperitivo with locals.

landmarks: Via Garibaldi and the Palazzi dei Rolli
A UNESCO-listed Renaissance street of gold-frescoed aristocratic palaces, including the Palazzo Rosso and Palazzo Bianco art museums of the Strada Nuova.
Genoa Cathedral (Cattedrale di San Lorenzo)
Striped in black-and-white marble, this Romanesque-Gothic cathedral guards the Holy Grail chalice and an unexploded British shell from 1941.
Acquario di Genova
Europe's largest aquarium anchors the revamped Old Port, its 70 tanks of sharks, dolphins and manatees designed within Renzo Piano's waterfront masterplan.
Porto Antico and the Bigo
Renzo Piano transformed Genoa's ancient harbour into a lively promenade crowned by the Bigo panoramic lift, mimicking the derricks of old cargo ships.
Piazza De Ferrari
Genoa's grand central square rings a great bronze fountain with the Art Nouveau stock exchange, opera house and Palazzo Ducale.
The Caruggi (Historic Centre Alleys)
One of Europe's largest medieval old towns, this shadowy maze of alleys hides Baroque churches, friggitorie and Via del Campo of De André fame.
La Lanterna
The 77-metre medieval lighthouse, rebuilt in 1543, has guided sailors for centuries and remains the proud emblem of Italy's greatest port city.
Spianata Castelletto
An Art Nouveau lift rises from the old town to this beloved balcony terrace, where all Genoa's slate roofs, domes and harbour spread beneath you.
Boccadasse
A tiny pastel fishing cove tucked at the end of Corso Italia, where gelato-licking locals crowd a pebble beach beneath faded ochre houses.
Staglieno Monumental Cemetery
A hauntingly beautiful open-air museum of 19th-century funerary sculpture, its marble mourners and angels among the finest in Europe.

train.note: Genoa has no direct international trains. Genova Piazza Principe and Brignole are the main stations, with Trenitalia and Italo high-speed services to Milan (~1h30), Turin (~1h45), Rome (~4h), and Pisa/Florence, plus the scenic coastal regional line west to Ventimiglia on the French border (change there for Nice) and east through the Cinque Terre to La Spezia.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches (Flixbus, Itabus) use the Autostazione at Piazza della Vittoria, serving cities across Italy and international routes toward France and beyond.

ferry.note: The Port of Genoa is one of the Mediterranean's great ferry hubs. GNV, Grimaldi Lines, Moby, and Tirrenia sail to Sardinia (Porto Torres, Olbia), Sicily (Palermo), and Corsica (Bastia), plus international routes to Barcelona and Tunis, from the Stazione Marittima and Terminal Traghetti.

full.blurb: The five cliff-clinging villages of the Ligurian coast, linked by train and hiking trails, about 1h30 from Genoa - the region's must-do.
full.name: Cinque Terre

full.blurb: A colourful UNESCO harbour town at the tip of the gulf near La Spezia, gateway to the eastern Riviera.
full.name: Portovenere & La Spezia

full.blurb: The elegant Baroque former royal capital with its arcades, museums, and the Mole Antonelliana, about 1h45 by fast train.
full.name: Turin

half.blurb: The glamorous fishing-village harbour of Portofino and its elegant neighbour, about 40 min by train then boat or bus along the Riviera.
half.name: Portofino & Santa Margherita Ligure

half.blurb: A quieter pastel-fronted fishing town with a pebble beach and the San Fruttuoso abbey reachable by boat, about 40 min east.
half.name: Camogli

half.blurb: Genoa's own seaside district with a cliff-top passeggiata, seaside parks, and Liberty villas, about 15 min by train.
half.name: Nervi
